Definition: of Hebrew origin (H836); Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe:--Aser.
BiblicalUsage: Aser is Asher in the Greek spelling, and the name turns up twice in the New Testament. Anna the prophetess is of the tribe of Aser, an old widow who serves God with fastings and prayers night and day; and twelve thousand of the tribe of Aser are sealed among the servants of God.
TheologicalSignificance: A tribe named for a prophetess and for the sealed tells me that Asher's blessing has not run out: the tribe that was promised bread and royal dainties still has a widow praying in the temple, and a sealed remnant in the last days.
